title: Pasta with Tomato-Based Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and seafood is a home recipe that pairs spaghetti or linguine with a fragrant sauce made from tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, basil, and a mix of seafood such as shrimp, mussels, and calamari. The dish is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, and antioxidants, and can be easily adapted to personal taste preferences.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fresh‑tomato sauce contains lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Seafood provides high‑quality omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for cardiovascular health.
The tradition of pairing pasta with seafood originated in Italy’s coastal regions where fresh fish was abundant.
Adding a splash of red wine to the sauce deepens its flavor.
Cooking pasta al dente helps it hold onto the sauce, resulting in a more cohesive dish.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Heart support
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids from seafood help lower triglycerides and promote vascular health.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and vitamin C combat free radicals, reducing oxidative stress.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and pasta provide thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Seafood delivers zinc, selenium, and iodine, important for immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauce can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake in check.

items.title: Food toxins
items.content: Improperly stored seafood may contain histamine or other toxins.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of seafood can cause heaviness for people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the sauce and seafood. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, and a drizzle of olive oil. The dish pairs well with a light arugula or mixed‑green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat the sauce gently over low heat, adding a splash of water or broth to restore the desired consistency.
